Two dashboard photos as proof.

what_to_steal: The unit-economics proof for LC's clipping pilot: $430 → $4K is the story LC tells internally to fund its own clipper army. 'Faceless' is key — LC's product clips don't need faces, just hands + jewelry.

hook: "Currently at 60 clippers now" + '$430' + '10X return' — the multiple is the hook this time.

sequencing: Scale: 60 clippers.
Economics: $430 spend, ~10X return.
Reach: 1M+ views/month.

Two photos.

what_to_steal: The reframe lesson: '10X return' travels further than '$4K revenue' for the same result — LC reports its clipping pilot as a multiple internally.

hook: "clippers in the house, @blknoiz06 just drop a clipping campaign" — in-group call + '$10,000 in $ANSEM reward every month'.
body: The announcement: @blknoiz06 dropped a clipping campaign with $10,000 in $ANSEM rewards every month for clippers. Requirements: brand-new account + 5 posted clips for review, OR an existing account with 850+ followers and 1.5M views in the last 30 days. Plus: Kick is running a program paying $400 per 1M views. Call to tag clippers.
cta: "tag any clipper in the cs if yk one" — recruitment via tagging; 'bulls in control 🐂🀄️' community sign-off.
idea: A $10K/month $ANSEM token reward pool for clippers, gated by account requirements (new account + 5 clips, or 850+ followers / 1.5M views/30d) — plus Kick's $400-per-1M-views program as a second payout lane.
sequencing: In-group hook: clippers in the house.
The drop: $10K/month $ANSEM rewards.
Requirement path A: new account + 5 clips for review.
Requirement path B: 850+ followers + 1.5M views/30d.
Bonus lane: Kick pays $400 per 1M views.
CTA: tag a clipper.
Photo.
formatting: Campaign-announcement post with a photo (likely the rewards graphic). Requirements as a quoted block; crypto-community voice.
why_it_works: A fixed monthly pool ($10K) is simpler to market than per-view math, and the dual entry path recruits both hungry newcomers and proven accounts. Tagging turns recruitment into distribution.
what_to_steal: The dual-gate requirement design (prove yourself with 5 clips OR show existing reach) is LC's clipper onboarding filter. The monthly reward pool structure gives LC a template: fixed monthly clipper prize pool instead of per-view accounting.

hook: "doordash did $13.7 BILLION in revenue last year" — scale contrast sets up the '$20,000 campaign' punchline.
cta: "no need to thank me for the sauce (:" — casual value-drop close.
idea: DoorDash's CringeMart stunt (live billboards with a real-time embarrassing-purchase counter) was amplified by a $20K clipping campaign on Content Rewards — because a billboard reaches thousands while clips reach millions, and a $13.7B company runs clipping because the per-view math beats billboards.
sequencing: Scale hook: DoorDash $13.7B revenue.
The stunt: CringeMart live billboards — a condom every 37 seconds as landmark.
The praise: dashboard number made landmark — brilliant.
The reveal: the $20K Content Rewards clipping campaign you missed.
The math: billboard thousands vs clips millions.
The thesis: overspend making, underspend distributing — even $13.7B companies do the per-view math.
Close: if DoorDash does this, you should too.
formatting: Story-driven analysis: DoorDash case study with dashboard-number color (a condom every 37 seconds), two photos, then the clipping reveal and the 'brands get this wrong' thesis.
why_it_works: 'Here's what you all missed' creates insider status for the reader. The $13.7B-vs-$20K contrast demolishes the 'clipping is for small brands' objection in one line.
what_to_steal: The budget-ratio thesis for LC: shift spend from production to distribution — LC's dupe machine IS the clipping campaign. The 'dashboard number as landmark' trick is stealable for LC organic ('a tarnish-free piece sells every X seconds').

hook: "this instagram page made me almost $10k in the last 30 days. every video i post makes me $300+" — personal earnings as proof.
cta: none explicit — the playbook is the content; implied CTA is to start clipping.
idea: The clipper-side playbook: cut the best moments from streamers'/YouTubers' videos, add hooks/captions, post as shorts, submit links to clipping campaigns (Content Rewards, Clipping Net, Clipster) paying ~$3K per 1M views — unlimited accounts, unlimited posts.
sequencing: Earnings hook: ~$10K/30 days, $300+ per video at $3K per 1M views.
The workflow: cut streamers' best moments, add hooks/captions, post, submit link, earn.
The clarification: Instagram doesn't pay — the campaign platform does.
The shortlist: Content Rewards, Clipping Net, Clipster.
The steps: pick campaign, read requirements, download, edit, post, earn — unlimited posts/accounts.
The kicker: 1M views = rent paid.
formatting: Clipper-side earnings flex: personal revenue claim ($10K/30 days), the $3K-per-1M-views rate, a numbered workflow, and the 3-platform shortlist. Two photos.
why_it_works: Personal earnings ('my page made $10K') beat platform promises. The step-by-step is dead simple, which is the point — low friction is why the supply side scales.
what_to_steal: The clipper-motivation intel for LC's campaign design: clippers want simple submission (copy link → submit), clear per-view rates, and no account limits. LC's clipper brief should mirror this: 'cut our best moments, add your hook, submit the link.'

hook: "I ran a clipping campaign at 10X ROAS previously. Here's exactly how I did it:" — the multiple + the exact-how promise.
body: The exact playbook: paid $0.20-$0.60 CPM by country; sourced clippers directly from TikTok; each clipper posted 2-3 TikTok slides in the given format; app logo + name inside the CTA slide of EVERY creative for brand recognition (so later paid ads convert better on subconscious familiarity); every clipper tags the app account in each post bio; alt accounts comment as users ('yo this app is so good'). Management: Discord DIY or rev-share agency (recommended — they handle recruiting, tracking, scaling). Offer to intro a 'cracked' agency.
cta: "If you want a cracked agency, hit me up I'll intro you to him." — warm-intro offer.
idea: The 10X ROAS clipping blueprint: $0.20-$0.60 CPMs, TikTok-sourced clippers, 2-3 slides each, logo in every CTA slide for brand-recognition compounding, bio tags, alt-account social proof comments, and agency management on rev share.
sequencing: Hook: 10X ROAS, exact how-to.
The setup: $0.20-$0.60 CPMs, TikTok-sourced clippers, 2-3 slides each.
The 'huge' insight: logo + name in EVERY CTA slide.
The mechanism: recognition compounding makes later paid ads convert better.
The extras: bio tags on every post + alt-account social-proof comments.
Management: rev-share agency recommended over Discord DIY.
CTA: intro to the cracked agency.
formatting: How-I-did-it playbook: bullet economics, the logo-in-CTA-slide insight called out as 'huge', management advice, intro offer. 170 bookmarks — operator gold.
why_it_works: 'That last part is huge' flags the non-obvious insight (brand recognition compounding) inside a tactical list — the reader gets both the how and the why. Exact CPMs make it feel real.
what_to_steal: The logo-in-every-CTA-slide rule is the single best insight: LC's watermark/logo on every clipper slide builds recognition that compounds into paid. The $0.20-$0.60 CPM benchmark, TikTok sourcing, and rev-share agency management are LC's clipping ops template.

The take: most do UGC/influencers, but clippers are 'the new meta'; with AI apps buildable from a prompt, run a clipping campaign and print views immediately. 18s video.
cta: none explicit — the thesis is the close ('clippers are the new meta').
idea: A peptides app hit $25K/mo by running a Content Rewards clipping campaign where clippers spammed AI before/after slideshows to 20M views — clippers are the new meta for app distribution.
sequencing: Hook: $0 → $25K/mo, most underrated strategy.
The chain: peptides app → CR clipping campaign → clippers joined.
The content: AI before/after slideshows, spammed.
The result: 20M views.
The contrast: everyone does UGC/influencers; clippers are the new meta.
The enabler: apps buildable from one prompt now.
The prescription: run a clipping campaign, print views.
18s video.

why_it_works: The arrow chain (→) makes a complex outcome feel like an inevitable sequence. '$0 to $25K' + '20M views' are the only numbers needed — the story sells itself.
what_to_steal: The AI-slideshow-as-clipper-content proof: clippers don't need original footage — AI before/after slideshows drove 20M views. LC's clippers can post AI jewelry transformation slideshows (tarnished → pristine) with zero filming.

The math: $10/post × 2/day = $600/mo per creator.

The recruitment: join link in comments.
Photo.

hook: "this app spams ONE format and pulled 522M views with organic UGC" — one format + 522M views is the whole hook.
body: The Musa case: a period/pregnancy app that spams ONE format — a 4-second shocked reaction to a body fact 'nobody told you,' then the dragon mascot in the app explains it. 522M views, 930 videos past 100K views, top video 12.2M, 100+ creators all running the same hook. Link to browse the full UGC operation on darkugc.com. 8s video + photo.
cta: "you can check their entire UGC operation here for free" + darkugc.com link — research-tool plug.
idea: Musa's 522M-view engine: 100+ creators all running ONE format — 4s shocked reaction to an untold body fact, then the in-app dragon mascot explains it — proving single-format spam at creator scale beats format variety.
sequencing: Hook: ONE format, 522M views, organic UGC.
The format: 4s shocked reaction to a period fact nobody told you.
The payoff: the dragon mascot explains it.
The numbers: 930 videos >100K, top 12.2M.
The scale: 100+ creators, same hook.
The research: full UGC operation on darkugc.com.
8s video + photo.
formatting: One-format case study: the format described in one line, the numbers stacked (522M, 930, 12.2M, 100+), 8s video + photo, research-link close.
why_it_works: 'Spams ONE format' is heresy against variety advice — the contrarian frame plus 522M views makes it undeniable. The mascot-explains payoff gives every video a consistent branded close.
what_to_steal: The one-format-spam doctrine as LC's counter-strategy: pick ONE winning jewelry format (e.g., 4s shocked reaction to 'your jewelry is turning your skin green' → LC piece explains waterproof) and run it across 100+ creators. This is the strongest evidence in the library for format concentration over variety.
